purpose: One Error System Lib: boot-safe reporting, unified outcome and independent Error/Log buffer responsibilities. Clearly separate user-confirmed facts from proposed implementation choices.

confirmed.rule: Error is a shared System Lib, available from BOOT through Core/System/User modules, not owned by HC.CS and not a sixth Hardcore mechanism.
CS is input; CSo is plain OK for no-data success, actual command return data for success with data, or unified ERROR for failure.
All components use the same Error mechanism; a non-CS Error must not invent a CS invocation.
Every Error during a CS invocation produces one CS command+parameters Log Buffer record, even with normal logging off, and it is not duplicated when already logged.
Any Error includes available actor identity when AC is active regardless of logging mode.
Normal CS logging modes off (default), cs and ac. Mode cs requires CS; ac requires CS and AccessCore.
Both buffers are configured from config.json independently, where N>=1 retains newest N and 0 retains all entries.

effects: append to Error Buffer exactly once
if a real CS invocation is in context, ensure one command+parameter Log Buffer record
API.propagation: forward same Error identity; don't emit new Error on catching/rethrowing the same failure

architecture.Error: System Lib with no HC.CS or AC import
architecture.Logger: shared minimal logging sink even in off (candidate System Lib), receives CS data/actor via argument, not HC.CS/AC import
architecture.optional_import: ERROR -> LOGGING, if direct lib import is chosen; alternative registered sink injection remains OPEN
architecture.sources: HC.CS and BOOT use ERROR; selected cs/ac success capture uses optional CS-side hook; thus no ERROR <-> HC.CS cycle
architecture.semantic_vs_import_dependency: Mode cs/ac capability requirements are NOT proof of Logger-to-CS Python imports

buffer_ownership.legacy: Do not store diagnostically owned truth wholesale under #SYSTEM / $SYSTEM.ERRORS

bootstrap.before_config: Error works before config.json and CS startup
bootstrap.capture: temporary minimal boot-safe Error receiver; exact capacity and merge behavior OPEN
bootstrap.config: BOOT validates protected config then supplies settings to libraries; libraries do not give CS read access to /config

buffer_lifecycle.default_storage: volatile MEM, aligned with 1.9 baseline (buffer-specific choice not yet confirmed)
buffer_lifecycle.FILE: No implicit persistence; optional explicit FILE backend/exports OPEN
buffer_lifecycle.N_positive: on append, drop oldest only after reaching configured N
buffer_lifecycle.N_zero: no count-based eviction; never silently reinterpret zero as off
buffer_lifecycle.resize: proposed keep newest on shrink; lost entries not reconstructed on grow
buffer_lifecycle.security: retain useful command/parameter context while masking secrets; detailed policy OPEN

failure_behavior.logging_failure: Original Error remains observable; no recursive Error->Logger->Error reentry
failure_behavior.concurrency: Use explicit context for invocation/AC identity; global mutable actor is unsafe under CP concurrency
failure_behavior.correlation: lightweight invocation identity proposed, exact ABI OPEN

candidate_NOT_YET_USER_APPROVED.result_ambiguity: Internal typed outcome may be necessary when command success data literally equals OK or ERROR; CSo public success data remains unwrapped. No decision yet.
